# Client Profile — vAPI Network

_Researched 2026-09-20. Every claim below is sourced. Anything unsourced is marked
`[UNVERIFIED — ask on the call]`._

## What they actually are

**vAPI Network** (`vapinetwork.ai`) — positioning line on the homepage:
> "Onchain task market for agents and humans."

They are **not** `vapi.ai`, the voice-AI company. See "The name problem" below — this
is the single biggest LinkedIn-specific issue and our opening insight on the call.

### The product, in plain English
An open-source, **non-custodial TypeScript toolkit** that lets a person or an AI agent
discover and pay for APIs using one wallet, over the **x402** payment protocol.
From the GitHub repo:
> "One wallet, every x402 API. Non-custodial agent client, MCP server, CLI and gateway
> for Call, Tasks and Compute."

### The four products and their real status
| Product | What it does | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Call** | Finds x402 APIs, reads the live price, asks the buyer to approve that USDC amount, pays the service directly | **Live today** |
| **Tasks** | Post scoped work, fund it in USDC escrow, review the result before payment. Disputes go to 3 reviewers; 2 matching votes release, refund or split | Next / coming soon |
| **Compute** | — | Roadmap |
| **Stake** | — | Coming soon |

**This matters for content:** only *Call* ships today. Our content calendar must not
imply Tasks/Compute/Stake are live. Pre-launch products get "building in public"
treatment (roadmap, design decisions, waitlist), not "buy now" treatment.

### Technical facts we can safely say in content
- Non-custodial. Private key generated locally, encrypted under a passphrase, **never leaves the machine**.
- Spend policy applied **before** signing. Caps per wallet, per call, and per day.
- Payments route **directly** from the local wallet to the service — vAPI does not hold funds or proxy payments.
- Receipts written to a **local append-only ledger**. No telemetry off the machine by default.
- **Security audit completed by Hacken.**
- **Apache 2.0**, open source.
- Chains: EVM (Base mainnet, Arc testnet) and Solana. Settlement in **USDC**.
- Interfaces: `vapi` CLI, **MCP server** (works with Claude, Claude Desktop, Cursor),
  TypeScript SDK (`@vapi-network/core`, `@vapi-network/sources`), gateway (`vapi serve`, preview).
- Roadmap: local gateway daemon with per-key budgets, OpenTelemetry tracing,
  task/compute payment tools, discovery expansion (x402scan, Coinbase Bazaar).

### The category tailwind (our credibility ammunition)
x402 is not a fringe standard, and this is the fact that makes the whole thing
legible to a LinkedIn B2B audience:
- Launched by **Coinbase**, May 2025.
- **x402 Foundation** formed with Cloudflare, 2025. Core members include
  **Google, Visa, AWS, Circle, Anthropic, Vercel**.
- Governance moved to the **Linux Foundation, April 2026** — 22 launch members
  including Google, Visa, **Mastercard, Stripe**, AWS, Circle.
- Coinbase reported **69,000 active agents and 165M transactions** by late April 2026.
- >80% of x402 payments settle on **Base**, almost all in **USDC**.

## The name problem (open the meeting with this)

`vapi.ai` is a different, much larger company: voice-AI infrastructure, YC W21,
**$50M Series B led by Peak XV announced May 2026** ($72M total), 1M+ developers,
2.7M agents created, 1B+ calls.

Consequences on LinkedIn specifically:
- LinkedIn search is heavily name-match weighted. Typing "VAPI" surfaces the voice-AI
  company and jobs in Vapi, Gujarat. vAPI Network is invisible.
- Any "VAPI" hashtag or mention is diluted by a company with orders of magnitude more volume.
- Prospects who Google after seeing a post land on the wrong company.

**Mitigations we propose (Week 0, costs nothing, immediate):**
1. Company page name is **"vAPI Network"** — never "VAPI" alone. Tagline carries
   "onchain task market" so the preview card disambiguates.
2. **Every post's first line** and **every image watermark** uses "vAPI Network".
3. Own a distinct hashtag set (`#x402`, `#agenticpayments`, `#agenteconomy`) rather
   than `#vapi`.
4. Secure the LinkedIn page custom URL/handle now, before someone else does.
5. Consistent bio line across every employee profile so the page gains name authority.

`[UNVERIFIED — ask on the call]` Is a rebrand or name change on the table? It changes
how hard we push name-building vs. category-building.

## What we still need from them
- Does a LinkedIn company page exist already, or is it genuinely zero?
- Which founders/execs will post from **personal** profiles? (See `kpi-framework.md` —
  this is the #1 determinant of whether the numbers land.)
- Brand assets: logo files, fonts, colour hexes, any existing deck.
- Who approves content, and how fast? (Target: 48h turnaround.)
- Is there a token, a raise, or a Tasks launch date in the next 90 days? Those are
  content moments we'd build the calendar around.
- Do we get access to the founders for podcast hosting, or are we producing only?

## Sources
- https://vapinetwork.ai/
- https://github.com/vAPI-Network/vapi-network
- https://x.com/vAPI_Network
- https://www.alchemy.com/blog/how-x402-brings-real-time-crypto-payments-to-the-web
- https://www.leadrpro.com/blog/vapi-s-50m-raise-puts-voice-ai-into-b2b-lead-generation
- https://vapi.ai/
EOF
echo "written: $(wc -l < 01-strategy/client-profile.md) lines"

## The strategic bet

**Every competitor in agentic payments is fighting on Crypto Twitter. Nobody is on LinkedIn.**

That's not an accident — it's a gap. CT rewards speed, memes and token speculation.
LinkedIn rewards credibility, and it's where the people who can authorise a company to
route real money through agent infrastructure actually are: heads of platform, VPs of
engineering, ops and automation leads, CFOs, agency owners.

x402 now has Google, Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, AWS and Circle behind it under Linux
Foundation governance. That is a **LinkedIn story**, not a CT story. It's the story that
turns "crypto thing" into "payments standard my board has heard of."

So: **we do not try to out-CT anyone. We own the uncontested channel where the budget lives.**

## vAPI is a two-sided market — so we recruit both sides

This is the core of the brief: "bring B2B businesses so they can bring recruitment to
the platform." A task market is dead without both supply and demand. LinkedIn content
must be deliberately split.

### ICP A — DEMAND (the buyers: post tasks, route agent spend)
| | |
|---|---|
| **Titles** | Head of Automation / AI, Head of Platform, VP Engineering, CTO at 20–500 person B2B SaaS; Ops Directors; agency owners running delivery teams |
| **Geo** | US, UK, NL/DACH, Singapore |
| **The pain** | Their agents need to buy things — data, APIs, compute, human review — and there is no clean way to let a bot spend money with a spend cap and an audit trail. Today it's a shared corporate card, a spreadsheet, and anxiety. |
| **What they fear** | An autonomous process with access to funds. Unbounded spend. No receipts. Compliance asking "who approved this." |
| **What converts them** | Spend caps enforced before signing. Local append-only receipt ledger. Non-custodial — key never leaves the machine. Hacken audit. Apache 2.0. |
| **Where they hang out** | LinkedIn, Hacker News, dev podcasts, r/LocalLLaMA-adjacent. Not CT. |

### ICP B — SUPPLY (the sellers: list APIs, take tasks, get paid)
| | |
|---|---|
| **Titles** | API product owners, indie devs/dev shops, data providers, specialist agencies and high-skill freelancers |
| **The pain** | Monetising an API means Stripe, a billing page, a login wall, invoicing, chasing payment. For a $0.004 call that's absurd. |
| **What converts them** | Per-request payment with no accounts and no dashboards. Paid directly, instantly, in USDC. Discoverable by 69,000 agents. |
| **The hook** | "Your API can be bought by a machine at 3am for four-tenths of a cent, and you'll have the money before you wake up." |

### ICP C — AMPLIFIERS (not buyers, but they carry reach)
x402 ecosystem builders, Base/Coinbase devrel, AI-agent framework maintainers, MCP
builders, AI-infra analysts and newsletter writers. These are **podcast guests** and
comment-section allies, not sales targets. They are how a zero-follower page borrows
an audience — see `02-linkedin/engagement-playbook.md`.

> For teams building AI agents that need to buy things, **vAPI Network** is the
> non-custodial wallet and task market that lets an agent discover, pay for and
> commission work over x402 — with hard spend caps, direct settlement and a receipt
> for every transaction. Unlike custodial agent-payment platforms, **your key never
> leaves your machine and vAPI never holds your funds.**

## Message hierarchy (what we say, in priority order)

1. **Control** — "Spend policy is applied *before* signing. Caps per call, per wallet, per day."
2. **Custody** — "We never hold your funds. Payment goes from your wallet to the service."
3. **Proof** — "Every payment writes a receipt to a local append-only ledger."
4. **Legitimacy** — "x402 is governed by the Linux Foundation. Google, Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, AWS and Circle are members."
5. **Openness** — "Apache 2.0. Audited by Hacken. Read the code."
6. **The future** — "Tasks: fund scoped work in USDC escrow, review before you pay." _(pre-launch — build-in-public framing only)_

## Anti-positioning — what we never do
- Never lead with price action, tokens, airdrops or "wen." It kills the LinkedIn audience instantly.
- Never say "crypto" when "stablecoin settlement" or "programmable payments" is accurate.
- Never imply Tasks / Compute / Stake are live.
- Never use "VAPI" without "Network".
- No engagement-bait ("Agree? 👇"), no fake vulnerability posts, no broetry.

# Content Pillars

Five pillars. Every post maps to exactly one. The weekly mix is fixed so the feed
stays balanced and we never drift into all-product-all-the-time.

## Weekly mix (4 company posts + 3 founder posts per week)

| # | Pillar | Share | Job it does | ICP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The Agent Economy** | 30% | Category education. Make "agents that pay" normal and inevitable. | A + B |
| 2 | **Trust & Control** | 25% | Kill the "you want a bot to have my wallet?" objection before it's raised. | A |
| 3 | **Build in Public** | 20% | Roadmap, design decisions, what shipped, what broke. Earns dev credibility. | B + C |
| 4 | **Proof & People** | 15% | Podcast clips, guest insight, ecosystem voices, integrations. Borrowed authority. | All |
| 5 | **Supply-Side Pitch** | 10% | Direct "list your API / take tasks" recruitment. | B |

## Pillar detail

### 1. The Agent Economy
Why agents need their own money rails; what breaks when they don't have them;
x402 explained without jargon; the Linux Foundation / Visa / Mastercard legitimacy
story; MCP + payments; market data (69k active agents, 165M transactions, >80% on Base).

_Angle that works:_ "Your AI agent has a credit card problem." Start at the pain,
not the protocol.

### 2. Trust & Control
Spend caps before signing. Non-custodial key handling. The local append-only ledger.
Hacken audit. Apache 2.0. Threat modelling. "What happens if the agent goes rogue."

_Angle that works:_ Name the fear out loud, then answer it with a mechanism. This is
the pillar that converts sceptical enterprise readers, and it's where most crypto
companies are weakest.

### 3. Build in Public
What shipped this week. Why a design decision went the way it did. The gateway daemon,
per-key budgets, OpenTelemetry tracing. Honest "this is on the roadmap, not live yet"
posts about Tasks / Compute / Stake.

_Angle that works:_ Specific and slightly unflattering beats polished. "We rewrote the
spend-policy layer because the first version checked the cap *after* signing" is a
better post than "excited to announce."

### 4. Proof & People
Podcast episode announcements, clips, quote cards, takeaway carousels. Ecosystem
partner spotlights. Integration walkthroughs. Community contributions.

### 5. Supply-Side Pitch
"Monetise your API per request, no billing page." "Get paid in USDC, no invoice."
Walkthrough of listing a service. Earnings mechanics. Discovery via x402scan / Bazaar.

## Content formats and how often

| Format | Cadence | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Text + single image | 3×/wk | Highest reliability, fastest to produce |
| Carousel (PDF, 6–10 slides) | 1×/wk | Best dwell time on LinkedIn; the workhorse for education |
| Video clip (0:45–1:30, captioned, 1:1 or 4:5) | 1–2×/wk | Podcast-derived, zero marginal cost |
| Text-only founder post | 2×/wk | Founder profiles outperform pages; no asset needed |
| Document/report (lead magnet) | 1× per month, from M2 | Converts reach → email → conversation |
| Poll | 1× per fortnight | Cheap reach + genuine ICP research |

## Hard rules
- One idea per post. If it needs two, it's two posts.
- Hook in the first 2 lines — LinkedIn truncates at ~3 lines on mobile before "see more".
- No outbound links in the post body. Link goes in the first comment, always.
- 3–5 hashtags, at the end. Never `#vapi`.
- Every post ends with a question or a concrete next step, never "thoughts?".
- Claims get sources. If we can't source it, we don't post it.
EOF
cat > 01-strategy/voice-and-tone.md <<'EOF'
# Voice & Tone

## The voice in one line
**A senior engineer explaining something they genuinely find interesting, to a smart
person who doesn't work in crypto.**

Calm, specific, technically literate, allergic to hype. The credibility comes from
precision, not enthusiasm.

## Rules

**Do**
- Short sentences. Concrete nouns. Real numbers with sources.
- Lead with the problem the reader already has, not the product.
- Say the mechanism: "spend policy is applied before signing" beats "secure by design".
- Admit what isn't built yet. Pre-launch honesty is a trust asset for this ICP.
- Use "you" and "we". Never "one" or the passive voice.

**Don't**
- No emoji as bullets. One in a sign-off at most.
- No "🚀", "gm", "wagmi", "ser", "bullish", "wen", or any token/price talk.
- No "excited to announce" / "thrilled to share" / "game-changer" / "revolutionary" / "unlock".
- No broetry (one-line paragraphs stacked for drama).
- No engagement bait. No "comment X and I'll DM you" until we've earned the audience.
- Never say "crypto" where "stablecoin settlement" or "programmable payments" is accurate.
- Never "VAPI" alone. Always "vAPI Network".

## Two registers

**Company page** — institutional, precise, slightly formal. Explains the category.
This is the register that survives a compliance reader.

**Founder profile** — first person, opinionated, shows the work. Allowed to be blunt
("most agent-payment tools are custodial and nobody says so out loud"). This is where
reach actually comes from.

## Hook patterns that work for this ICP
1. **The uncomfortable question** — "Would you give an autonomous process your company card?"
2. **The specific number** — "165 million agent payments happened last year. Almost none of them had a spend cap."
3. **The correction** — "x402 isn't a crypto project. It's governed by the Linux Foundation, and Visa and Mastercard are members."
4. **The build note** — "We shipped the spend-policy layer twice. Here's what the first version got wrong."
5. **The concrete scene** — "At 3am a machine bought four-tenths of a cent of data from an API in Lisbon. Nobody logged in."

## Banned words
excited, thrilled, delighted, game-changer, revolutionary, disrupt, unlock, leverage,
seamless, robust, cutting-edge, synergy, best-in-class, paradigm, journey, ecosystem
(as filler), "the future of X is here".
EOF

| 5 | **Supply-Side Pitch** | 10% | Direct "list your API / take tasks" recruitment. | B |

## Pillar detail

### 1. The Agent Economy
Why agents need their own money rails; what breaks when they don't have them;
x402 explained without jargon; the Linux Foundation / Visa / Mastercard legitimacy
story; MCP + payments; market data (69k active agents, 165M transactions, >80% on Base).

_Angle that works:_ "Your AI agent has a credit card problem." Start at the pain,
not the protocol.

### 2. Trust & Control
Spend caps before signing. Non-custodial key handling. The local append-only ledger.
Hacken audit. Apache 2.0. Threat modelling. "What happens if the agent goes rogue."

_Angle that works:_ Name the fear out loud, then answer it with a mechanism. This is
the pillar that converts sceptical enterprise readers, and it's where most crypto
companies are weakest.

### 3. Build in Public
What shipped this week. Why a design decision went the way it did. The gateway daemon,
per-key budgets, OpenTelemetry tracing. Honest "this is on the roadmap, not live yet"
posts about Tasks / Compute / Stake.

_Angle that works:_ Specific and slightly unflattering beats polished. "We rewrote the
spend-policy layer because the first version checked the cap *after* signing" is a
better post than "excited to announce."

### 4. Proof & People
Podcast episode announcements, clips, quote cards, takeaway carousels. Ecosystem
partner spotlights. Integration walkthroughs. Community contributions.

### 5. Supply-Side Pitch
"Monetise your API per request, no billing page." "Get paid in USDC, no invoice."
Walkthrough of listing a service. Earnings mechanics. Discovery via x402scan / Bazaar.

## Content formats and how often

| Format | Cadence | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Text + single image | 3×/wk | Highest reliability, fastest to produce |
| Carousel (PDF, 6–10 slides) | 1×/wk | Best dwell time on LinkedIn; the workhorse for education |
| Video clip (0:45–1:30, captioned, 1:1 or 4:5) | 1–2×/wk | Podcast-derived, zero marginal cost |
| Text-only founder post | 2×/wk | Founder profiles outperform pages; no asset needed |
| Document/report (lead magnet) | 1× per month, from M2 | Converts reach → email → conversation |
| Poll | 1× per fortnight | Cheap reach + genuine ICP research |

## Hard rules
- One idea per post. If it needs two, it's two posts.
- Hook in the first 2 lines — LinkedIn truncates at ~3 lines on mobile before "see more".
- No outbound links in the post body. Link goes in the first comment, always.
- 3–5 hashtags, at the end. Never `#vapi`.
- Every post ends with a question or a concrete next step, never "thoughts?".
- Claims get sources. If we can't source it, we don't post it.
EOF

# Voice & Tone

## The voice in one line
**A senior engineer explaining something they genuinely find interesting, to a smart
person who doesn't work in crypto.**

Calm, specific, technically literate, allergic to hype. The credibility comes from
precision, not enthusiasm.

## Rules

**Do**
- Short sentences. Concrete nouns. Real numbers with sources.
- Lead with the problem the reader already has, not the product.
- Say the mechanism: "spend policy is applied before signing" beats "secure by design".
- Admit what isn't built yet. Pre-launch honesty is a trust asset for this ICP.
- Use "you" and "we". Never "one" or the passive voice.

**Don't**
- No emoji as bullets. One in a sign-off at most.
- No "🚀", "gm", "wagmi", "ser", "bullish", "wen", or any token/price talk.
- No "excited to announce" / "thrilled to share" / "game-changer" / "revolutionary" / "unlock".
- No broetry (one-line paragraphs stacked for drama).
- No engagement bait. No "comment X and I'll DM you" until we've earned the audience.
- Never say "crypto" where "stablecoin settlement" or "programmable payments" is accurate.
- Never "VAPI" alone. Always "vAPI Network".

## Two registers

**Company page** — institutional, precise, slightly formal. Explains the category.
This is the register that survives a compliance reader.

**Founder profile** — first person, opinionated, shows the work. Allowed to be blunt
("most agent-payment tools are custodial and nobody says so out loud"). This is where
reach actually comes from.

## Hook patterns that work for this ICP
1. **The uncomfortable question** — "Would you give an autonomous process your company card?"
2. **The specific number** — "165 million agent payments happened last year. Almost none of them had a spend cap."
3. **The correction** — "x402 isn't a crypto project. It's governed by the Linux Foundation, and Visa and Mastercard are members."
4. **The build note** — "We shipped the spend-policy layer twice. Here's what the first version got wrong."
5. **The concrete scene** — "At 3am a machine bought four-tenths of a cent of data from an API in Lisbon. Nobody logged in."

## Banned words
excited, thrilled, delighted, game-changer, revolutionary, disrupt, unlock, leverage,
seamless, robust, cutting-edge, synergy, best-in-class, paradigm, journey, ecosystem
(as filler), "the future of X is here".
EOF

# KPI Framework & Target Bands

## Read this first — the honest version

These are **target bands from a standing start**, not guarantees. State them on the
call exactly as written. Promising a number you can't control is how trials die in
month two.

Two things drive whether the top or bottom of each band lands, and only one is in our control:

1. **Founder/exec participation on personal profiles.** LinkedIn suppresses company-page
   reach hard — personal profiles routinely get 5–20× the reach of a page with the same
   follower count. A company page alone, from zero, with no employee amplification, is
   the single most common reason a B2B LinkedIn programme fails. **This is the one thing
   we need from them, and it should be stated as a condition, not a request.**
2. **Approval turnaround.** Content that sits in review for a week loses its news hook.
   We need 48h.

## Metric tiers

### Tier 1 — Leading (weekly; tells us if it's working before revenue does)
| Metric | Why | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Impressions | Total reach | Page analytics + per-post |
| Engagement rate | `(reactions+comments+shares)/impressions`. **Target >3%** — below 2% the hook is wrong | Per post |
| Comments from ICP titles | The real signal. 5 comments from Heads of Platform > 50 from bots | Manual tag in tracker |
| Profile/page views | Intent proxy | Analytics |
| Follower growth + **follower quality** | % of new followers matching ICP A or B | Analytics demographics |
| Saves & shares | Highest-value signals LinkedIn rewards | Per post |

### Tier 2 — Lagging (monthly; what they'll actually judge us on)
| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| Inbound conversations | Someone starts a DM or comment thread about using vAPI |
| Qualified conversations | That person matches ICP A or B |
| Demo / call booked | Calendar event exists |
| Email captures | From lead magnets, M2 onward |
| Supply-side signups | API providers or task-takers who joined because of LinkedIn |
| Attributed pipeline | Tagged in their CRM as LinkedIn-sourced |

### Tier 3 — Podcast
Downloads per episode, completion rate, clips published per episode (**target ≥8**),
guest→network conversion (how many guests or their companies end up on vAPI),
guest referral rate.

## 90-day target bands

| | Month 1 | Month 2 | Month 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Followers (page, from 0) | 300–600 | 800–1,500 | 1,500–3,000 |
| Monthly impressions | 8k–15k | 30k–60k | 60k–120k |
| Avg engagement rate | 2–4% (baseline) | 3–5% | 4–6% |
| Posts published | 28 | 30 | 30 |
| Podcast episodes live | 1 (pilot) | 3 | 6 |
| Inbound qualified convos | 0–3 | 3–8 | 10–25 |
| Booked calls / demos | 0–1 | 2–5 | 5–12 |
| Email list | — | 50–150 | 200–500 |

**Assumptions these bands depend on — say them out loud:**
- ≥2 founder/exec personal profiles post 2×/week and comment 10×/week.
- 48h content approval.
- Podcast starts by Week 3 with ≥1 recognisable ecosystem guest.
- No paid spend. (Bands are organic-only. £/$500–1,000/mo of Thought Leader Ads on
  the best-performing founder posts would roughly double the month-3 reach band —
  flag as an option, not a requirement.)

## What we report and when
- **Weekly (Mondays):** one-screen snapshot — top 3 posts, bottom 1 with the diagnosis,
  Tier 1 numbers vs. last week, what we're changing this week. Template in `05-ops/reporting/`.
- **Monthly:** full dashboard, Tier 1 + 2 + 3, what we learned, next month's plan,
  one explicit ask.
- **Day 90:** the retrospective and the renewal case.

## Kill criteria (build this into the trial — it makes us look confident)
If after 6 weeks engagement rate is still under 2% and qualified conversations are
zero, we stop and re-plan rather than keep shipping posts. Named in advance, this
reads as rigour. Unnamed, a bad month reads as failure.
EOF

# vAPI Network — 90-Day LinkedIn & Podcast Plan

_Prepared 2026-09-20 · Trial engagement · LinkedIn from zero → B2B pipeline_

---

## The thesis in four lines

1. vAPI Network is a **two-sided market**. LinkedIn must recruit buyers *and* sellers, deliberately, on a fixed ratio.
2. **Every competitor in agentic payments is on Crypto Twitter. LinkedIn is empty** — and it's where the people who authorise spend actually are.
3. The blocker isn't awareness, it's **trust**. "Let a bot spend money" needs a mechanism answer, not a marketing answer. vAPI has the mechanisms — spend caps before signing, non-custodial keys, a local receipt ledger, a Hacken audit. Most rivals don't.
4. The **podcast is the engine, not a side project.** One 45-minute recording becomes 8–12 LinkedIn assets and puts a founder in a room with exactly the people we want on the network.

---

## Phase 0 — Week 0: Foundation (before a single post)

Unglamorous and non-negotiable. Skipping it is why most LinkedIn launches stall at week five.

**Fix the name problem first.** `vapi.ai` — voice AI, YC W21, $50M Series B in May 2026, 1M+ developers — owns every "VAPI" search on LinkedIn. vAPI Network is currently invisible behind it.
- Page name: **"vAPI Network"**, never "VAPI" alone
- Tagline carries "onchain task market" so link previews disambiguate
- Claim the custom page URL immediately
- "vAPI Network" in every post's first line and every image watermark
- Own `#x402` / `#agenticpayments` / `#agenteconomy`, never `#vapi`

**Also in Week 0:**
- Company page built: banner, logo, tagline, About (keyword-weighted for "x402", "agent payments", "AI agent infrastructure"), Products, custom CTA button
- **Founder/exec profile overhauls** — headline, banner, About, Featured section. This is where the reach comes from; the page is the credibility backstop
- Brand kit: 6 Canva/Figma templates (quote card, stat card, carousel cover, carousel interior, clip frame, podcast announce) in vAPI's colours
- Analytics baseline + tracking sheet; UTM convention agreed
- 30-day content calendar approved in one batch, so weeks 1–4 never wait on sign-off
- Podcast: name, cover art, format, first 10 guest targets, recording stack

**Deliverables:** optimised page, 2–3 optimised profiles, 6 design templates, 30-day calendar, podcast brand kit, tracking sheet.

---

## Month 1 — Foundation & Signal (Weeks 1–4)

**Goal:** publish consistently, establish the category voice, find out what the audience responds to. We are buying information this month, not leads.

**Cadence:** 4 company posts + 3 founder posts per week (28 posts total)

| Week | Focus | Notable |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Category education — "why agents need their own money rails" | Launch post; first carousel: *"x402 explained for people who don't do crypto"* |
| 2 | Trust & Control — spend caps, non-custodial keys, the receipt ledger | Poll: *"Would you let an autonomous agent spend from a company wallet?"* → doubles as ICP research |
| 3 | Build in Public — Call is live, what's real vs. roadmap | **Podcast pilot records.** First supply-side post: "monetise your API per request" |
| 4 | Proof & People — ecosystem, the Linux Foundation legitimacy story | **Episode 1 publishes** + 8 derived assets. Month-1 report |

**Engagement (the half that nobody budgets for and everyone needs):**
Founders comment on 10 ICP/ecosystem posts per week — substantive, 2+ sentences, adding something. A zero-follower page grows by borrowing audiences in other people's comment sections. Target list maintained in `02-linkedin/engagement-playbook.md`.

**Month 1 targets:** 300–600 followers · 8–15k impressions · 2–4% engagement · baseline established

---

## Month 2 — Traction & Amplification (Weeks 5–8)

**Goal:** double down on what month 1 proved, and start converting reach into contacts.

- **Rebalance the calendar around the data.** Whichever pillar carried month 1 goes to 35–40%; the weakest drops.
- **Podcast to fortnightly rhythm** — episodes 2 and 3. Guests drawn from ICP C (x402 ecosystem builders, Base/Coinbase devrel, MCP and agent-framework maintainers). Every guest amplifies to their own audience: that is the growth mechanism.
- **First lead magnet:** *"The Agent Spend Control Checklist — 12 questions to ask before you let an AI agent touch money."* Gated, email capture, promoted across 3 posts. Deliberately vendor-neutral so it travels.
- **Video scales up** to 2 clips/week from podcast footage. Captioned, 4:5, hook in the first 1.5 seconds.
- **Employee advocacy:** simple repost/comment pack to the wider team each Monday.
- **First partner cross-post** with an ecosystem project.
- **Supply-side push:** a dedicated week-7 sequence aimed at API providers and dev shops.

**Month 2 targets:** 800–1,500 followers · 30–60k impressions · 3–5% engagement · 3–8 qualified conversations · 50–150 emails

---

## Month 3 — Conversion & Compounding (Weeks 9–12)

**Goal:** turn an audience into pipeline, and hand over a system that runs without heroics.

- **Conversion layer:** warm-DM playbook (never cold-pitch; reference their comment or a post they engaged with), founder "open calendar" post, a clear route from post → first comment → booked call.

# Objection Handling

Format: what they say → what's really being asked → the answer. Keep answers short and
mechanism-led. Never argue.

---

**"How do we know this will actually generate leads?"**
_Real question: are you going to waste our money?_
> "You don't yet, and I won't pretend otherwise from a zero-follower start. What I can
> commit to is the leading indicators — engagement rate above 3% and comments from the
> right job titles — inside four weeks. Those precede pipeline reliably. And we've set
> a kill criterion: if at week six engagement is under 2% with zero qualified
> conversations, we stop and re-plan instead of billing you for posts."

---

**"Our audience is on Crypto Twitter, not LinkedIn."**
_Real question: is this the wrong channel?_
> "Your *developer* audience is on CT. Your *buyer* is not. The person who authorises a
> company to route real money through agent infrastructure is a head of platform or a
> CFO, and they're on LinkedIn. Also — that's exactly why it works. Every competitor is
> fighting for attention on CT. LinkedIn is uncontested. You'd be the only serious voice
> on agentic payments there."

---

**"$1,300 feels like a lot for social media."**
_Real question: what am I actually buying?_
> "It's not social media posting, it's 28–30 published assets a month, a produced
> podcast that doubles as a business-development channel, all the design, and the
> strategy behind it. A single mid-level marketing hire is ten times that and can't do
> the podcast. Compare it to one qualified enterprise conversation — if it produces one
> a month, it's paid for itself."

---

**"Why do our founders have to post? Can't you run the page?"**
_The one you must not soften._
> "I can run the page, and it'll underperform. LinkedIn deliberately suppresses company
> page reach — personal profiles get five to twenty times the reach at the same follower
> count. From zero, the page has no distribution to borrow. Founder profiles do.
>
> We make it a fifteen-minute job: we write it, you edit and post. But if founders won't
> post, I'd want to reset the targets down now rather than miss them later."

---

**"We can't talk about the roadmap publicly."**
> "Good — that keeps us honest. We'll only claim Call, which is live. Tasks, Compute and
> Stake get build-in-public framing: design decisions and problems, never launch dates
> you haven't set. That's actually stronger content for a developer audience than an
> announcement would be."

---

**"What if we get a negative or a compliance-sensitive comment?"**
> "There's an escalation protocol in the ops folder. Technical criticism gets answered
> in public with a mechanism — it's some of the best content we can produce. Anything
> touching regulation, custody or securities gets routed to you, not answered by us.
> We never freelance on compliance."

---

**"Can you guarantee X followers?"**
> "No, and anyone who does is either buying followers or guessing. I'll give you bands
> with the assumptions written down, and I'll tell you every week whether we're tracking
> to the top or the bottom of them and why."

---

**"We tried LinkedIn before and it didn't work."**
_Listen properly here — the answer is in their story._
> "What did the cadence look like, and were the founders posting?" — Nine times out of
> ten it was a company page, inconsistent, product announcements only. That's three
> fixable problems, and the plan addresses all three.

---

**"How fast can you start?"**
> "Week 0 starts Monday. First post live inside two weeks. The only thing that slows it
> is brand assets and picking an approver — both of which we can settle today."

---

**"Can you do more channels — X, YouTube, newsletter?"**
> "Yes, but not in this scope and not yet. Get one channel genuinely working first;
> everything we build here — the podcast especially — feeds the others for almost no
> extra cost. Let's revisit at day 90 with data rather than guesses."

---

**"Who actually does the work — is this all AI?"**
_Increasingly common. Answer it straight._
> "We use AI heavily for research, drafting and production volume — that's how the
> economics work at this price. Strategy, judgement, the guest relationships and every
> word that goes out are reviewed by a person. You're buying the system and the
> accountability, not the keystrokes."
EOF

# Discovery Questions

Ask these on the call. Answers go straight into `01-strategy/client-profile.md`.
Priority ★ = ask even if time is short.

## Commercial
- ★ Is this trial for vAPI Network directly, or are we subcontracting through the agency? Who signs off, who pays?
- ★ Is $1,300 per month, or one-off for the 90 days? _(This changes scope — see `scope-and-pricing.md`.)_
- What would make you say at day 90 that this worked? Be specific.
- Is there a budget for paid amplification on top, or is this strictly organic?
- Is VAPA the same buyer? Should the two run as one programme or stay separate?

## Product & truth
- ★ What ships in the next 90 days? Any date for Tasks?
- Is there a token, a raise, or a public launch we should build the calendar around?
- ★ Is a rebrand or name change on the table? _(Changes how hard we push name-building vs. category-building.)_
- Who are the real competitors in your view — and who do you not want mentioned?
- Anything legally off-limits? Securities language, custody claims, jurisdictions?

## Audience
- ★ Who are your best current users — buyers or API providers? Names and titles.
- Where do you get users today? What's actually working?
- Who do you most want to reach and currently can't?
- Any logos, numbers or user stories we're allowed to cite?

## Existing presence
- ★ Does a LinkedIn company page exist? Admin access?
- Who on the team posts already, and who's willing to start?
- Analytics access — page, site, CRM?
- What content exists we can repurpose — docs, talks, threads, decks?

## Podcast
- ★ Who hosts — a founder, or do we supply a host?
- Do you have 45 minutes every two weeks, reliably?
- Existing name, feed, or art — or are we starting clean?
- Who are the five guests you'd most want, and do you have a warm intro to any?
- Video as well as audio? (Strongly recommended — it's where the clips come from.)

## Brand & design
- ★ Logo files, fonts, colour hexes, existing deck — who sends them and when?
- Any brand guidelines document?
- Anything visually you actively dislike?

## Process
- ★ Who is the single named content approver, and can they turn things around in 48 hours?
- Preferred tools — Notion, Slack, Google Drive?
- How do you want to receive reporting, and how often?
- Who handles inbound DMs and comments — us, or you?
EOF

+> ten it was a company page, inconsistent, product announcements only. That's three
+> fixable problems, and the plan addresses all three.
+**"How fast can you start?"**
+> "Week 0 starts Monday. First post live inside two weeks. The only thing that slows it
+> is brand assets and picking an approver — both of which we can settle today."
+**"Can you do more channels — X, YouTube, newsletter?"**
+> "Yes, but not in this scope and not yet. Get one channel genuinely working first;
+> everything we build here — the podcast especially — feeds the others for almost no
+> extra cost. Let's revisit at day 90 with data rather than guesses."
+**"Who actually does the work — is this all AI?"**
+_Increasingly common. Answer it straight._
+> "We use AI heavily for research, drafting and production volume — that's how the
+> economics work at this price. Strategy, judgement, the guest relationships and every
+> word that goes out are reviewed by a person. You're buying the system and the
+> accountability, not the keystrokes."
+# Discovery Questions
+Ask these on the call. Answers go straight into `01-strategy/client-profile.md`.
+Priority ★ = ask even if time is short.
+## Commercial
+- ★ Is this trial for vAPI Network directly, or are we subcontracting through the agency? Who signs off, who pays?
+- ★ Is $1,300 per month, or one-off for the 90 days? _(This changes scope — see `scope-and-pricing.md`.)_
+- What would make you say at day 90 that this worked? Be specific.
+- Is there a budget for paid amplification on top, or is this strictly organic?
+- Is VAPA the same buyer? Should the two run as one programme or stay separate?
+## Product & truth
+- ★ What ships in the next 90 days? Any date for Tasks?
+- Is there a token, a raise, or a public launch we should build the calendar around?
+- ★ Is a rebrand or name change on the table? _(Changes how hard we push name-building vs. category-building.)_
+- Who are the real competitors in your view — and who do you not want mentioned?
+- Anything legally off-limits? Securities language, custody claims, jurisdictions?
+## Audience
+- ★ Who are your best current users — buyers or API providers? Names and titles.
+- Where do you get users today? What's actually working?
+- Who do you most want to reach and currently can't?
+- Any logos, numbers or user stories we're allowed to cite?
+## Existing presence
+- ★ Does a LinkedIn company page exist? Admin access?
+- Who on the team posts already, and who's willing to start?
+- Analytics access — page, site, CRM?
+- What content exists we can repurpose — docs, talks, threads, decks?
+## Podcast
+- ★ Who hosts — a founder, or do we supply a host?
+- Do you have 45 minutes every two weeks, reliably?
+- Existing name, feed, or art — or are we starting clean?
+- Who are the five guests you'd most want, and do you have a warm intro to any?
+- Video as well as audio? (Strongly recommended — it's where the clips come from.)
+## Brand & design
+- ★ Logo files, fonts, colour hexes, existing deck — who sends them and when?
+- Any brand guidelines document?
+- Anything visually you actively dislike?
+## Process
+- ★ Who is the single named content approver, and can they turn things around in 48 hours?
+- Preferred tools — Notion, Slack, Google Drive?
+- How do you want to receive reporting, and how often?
+- Who handles inbound DMs and comments — us, or you?

# Scope & Pricing

> **⚠ Assumption to confirm on the call.** The brief says "roughly $1,300 per project,"
> and VAPA is a separate project. This document assumes **$1,300 per month** for the
> vAPI Network engagement. If it's $1,300 for the whole 90 days, the scope below is
> roughly 3× too large — use the **Reduced Scope** column instead and say so plainly.
> **Settle this before talking deliverables.** Ask: _"Just so I scope this right — is
> the $1,300 monthly, or for the full trial?"_

---

## Monthly deliverables

| Deliverable | Full scope (~$1,300/mo) | Reduced (~$1,300 total for 90 days) |
|---|---|---|
| LinkedIn company posts | 16/mo (4/wk) | 8/mo (2/wk) |
| Founder-profile posts (ghostwritten) | 12/mo (3/wk across 2 profiles) | 4/mo |
| Carousels (6–10 slides) | 4/mo | 1/mo |
| Static graphics | 12–16/mo | 6/mo |
| Video clips (captioned, branded) | 6–8/mo | 2/mo |
| Podcast episodes produced | 2/mo | 1/mo |
| Podcast → clips + assets | 8–12 per episode | 4 per episode |
| Engagement/commenting support | Weekly target list + drafted comments | Target list only |
| Lead magnet | 1 per month from M2 | 1 total |
| Reporting | Weekly snapshot + monthly dashboard | Monthly only |
| Strategy calls | Weekly 30 min | Monthly 30 min |

**One-off, included in Week 0 either way:** page optimisation, 2–3 founder profile
overhauls, 6 design templates, podcast brand kit, tracking sheet, 30-day calendar.

---

## Explicitly out of scope _(say this before they ask)_

Quotable separately, at additional cost:
- Full brand identity or logo design
- Motion graphics / animated video
- Website design or copy
- Paid ad management and ad spend
- Other channels — X, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, newsletter
- Outbound prospecting / SDR work (we generate inbound; we don't cold-DM at volume)
- Event, conference or PR support
- Community management outside LinkedIn (Discord, Telegram)
- Podcast studio hire, travel, or in-person recording
- Translation / localisation

**Fair-use guard:** two rounds of revision per asset are included. Rewrites caused by a
change in product direction or positioning after approval are scoped separately — not
punitively, just so a pivot doesn't silently eat the month.

---

## Making the price defensible

Don't defend the number — reframe what it buys.

- **Per asset:** ~50 published assets a month at full scope is roughly **$26 per asset**, strategy, design and podcast production included.
- **Versus a hire:** a mid-level content marketer is $4–6k/month, can't produce a podcast, and takes a quarter to ramp.
- **Versus the outcome:** one qualified enterprise conversation with a platform lead covers it several times over.

---

## What to propose if they push back on price

In order of preference:

1. **Hold the price, narrow the scope.** Drop video clips or founder ghostwriting first — never drop cadence or the podcast. Consistency is the thing that works.
2. **Trial period, then review.** 30 days at the reduced scope, full scope from month 2 on agreed leading indicators. Low risk for them, and the indicators are ours to hit.
3. **Bundle vAPI + VAPA** at a combined rate with shared strategy overhead. Genuinely cheaper to deliver, so the discount is real rather than conceded.

**Never** discount by cutting posting frequency. A programme that posts twice a week
instead of four times doesn't cost half as much to run and doesn't produce half the
result — it produces almost none.

---

## Terms to agree on the call
- Payment: monthly in advance, net 7
- 30-day notice either side after the trial
- Content approval: 48 hours; unreturned = approved (protects the calendar)
- Client owns all final assets; we retain portfolio rights unless they object
- Access needed: LinkedIn page admin, brand assets, analytics
EOF

# Chat Map — one session per job

The point of this folder: **don't run everything in one endless chat.** Each recurring
job gets its own session, started with its own slash command, so context stays clean
and output stays consistent.

Each command lives in `.claude/commands/` at the repo root and is invoked by typing
`/name` at the start of a fresh session.

| Command | Job | When | Writes to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/weekly-content` | Plan + draft next week's 7 posts | Thursday | `02-linkedin/calendar/` + `post-bank/` |
| `/post-draft` | Draft one post on a specific angle | Ad hoc | `02-linkedin/post-bank/` |
| `/engage` | Build this week's commenting target list + draft comments | Monday | `02-linkedin/engagement-log.md` |
| `/podcast-prep` | Guest research, question set, pre-call brief | Before each recording | `03-podcast/episodes/` |
| `/podcast-repurpose` | Turn a transcript into 8–12 LinkedIn assets | After each episode | `03-podcast/episodes/` + `post-bank/` |
| `/design-brief` | Turn an approved post into a designer-ready asset brief | With each visual | `04-design/briefs/` |
| `/report` | Weekly snapshot or monthly dashboard | Monday / month-end | `05-ops/reporting/` |
| `/research` | Category, competitor or guest research with sources | Ad hoc | `01-strategy/` |

## Rules for every session
1. **One command, one job.** Don't drift — start a new session instead.
2. Claude reads `CLAUDE.md` automatically. It carries the voice rules and the
   no-invented-metrics rule, so output is consistent across sessions.
3. Everything lands in a file, not just in the chat. Chats get lost; files don't.
4. Every session is logged to `logs/` automatically — see `logs/README.md`.

## Weekly rhythm at a glance
```
MON  /engage    → target list + drafted comments        (30 min)
     /report    → last week's snapshot                  (20 min)
TUE  publish + live engagement
WED  publish · /podcast-prep if recording this week
THU  /weekly-content → next week's 7 posts drafted      (60 min)
     → send for approval (48h clock starts)
FRI  /design-brief for each approved visual             (30 min)
     /podcast-repurpose if an episode was recorded
```
EOF
cat > 05-ops/weekly-workflow.md <<'EOF'
# Weekly Operating Rhythm

Roughly 6–8 hours a week at full scope. The discipline that matters: **draft a week
ahead, always.** Same-day drafting is how quality collapses and how approval delays
turn into gaps in the feed.

## Monday — Review & Engage
- [ ] `/report` → weekly snapshot. Top 3 posts, worst post + diagnosis, Tier 1 numbers vs. last week
- [ ] `/engage` → 20 target posts to comment on, drafted comments for the founders
- [ ] Send founders their comment pack + their 2 posts for the week
- [ ] Check DMs and comments from last week; escalate anything compliance-adjacent
- [ ] Post #1 of the week goes live

## Tuesday — Publish & Respond
- [ ] Post #2 live
- [ ] **First 60 minutes after posting are the highest-leverage time of the week** — reply to every comment
- [ ] Founder posts go live
- [ ] Log early performance

## Wednesday — Publish & Produce
- [ ] Post #3 live (usually the carousel)
- [ ] Podcast recording if scheduled, or `/podcast-prep` for the next one
- [ ] Outreach to 3 new guest targets

## Thursday — Next Week's Content
- [ ] `/weekly-content` → draft all 7 posts for next week
- [ ] Self-edit against `01-strategy/voice-and-tone.md` — especially the banned-words list
- [ ] **Send for approval. 48h clock starts.**
- [ ] Post #4 live

## Friday — Design & Repurpose
- [ ] `/design-brief` for each approved visual
- [ ] Produce graphics from the master templates
- [ ] `/podcast-repurpose` if an episode was recorded
- [ ] Schedule next week where approved
- [ ] Update the tracking sheet

## Monthly (last Friday)
- [ ] Full dashboard — Tier 1, 2 and 3
- [ ] Pillar performance review → rebalance next month's mix
- [ ] Refresh the guest pipeline to 10 deep
- [ ] Lead magnet production (M2+)
- [ ] Client call: results, learnings, next month, one explicit ask

## Approval flow
1. Draft → `02-linkedin/post-bank/` marked `STATUS: draft`
2. Batch of 7 sent Thursday → `STATUS: in-review`
3. Approved → `STATUS: approved`, design brief raised
4. Scheduled → `STATUS: scheduled` + date
5. Published → `STATUS: live` + URL, performance logged after 72h

**Unreturned after 48h = approved.** Agreed up front so the calendar can't be blocked
by silence.

## Escalation — never freelance on these
Route to the client, don't answer: anything about regulation, securities, custody,
tax or jurisdiction · claims about funds safety we can't source · competitor disputes ·
anything involving a named individual · press enquiries.

Answer ourselves, in public, with a mechanism: technical criticism, "how does this
differ from X", scepticism about agent spending. These are our best content.
EOF

+- [ ] Post #2 live
+- [ ] **First 60 minutes after posting are the highest-leverage time of the week** — reply to every comment
+- [ ] Founder posts go live
+- [ ] Log early performance
+## Wednesday — Publish & Produce
+- [ ] Post #3 live (usually the carousel)
+- [ ] Podcast recording if scheduled, or `/podcast-prep` for the next one
+- [ ] Outreach to 3 new guest targets
+## Thursday — Next Week's Content
+- [ ] `/weekly-content` → draft all 7 posts for next week
+- [ ] Self-edit against `01-strategy/voice-and-tone.md` — especially the banned-words list
+- [ ] **Send for approval. 48h clock starts.**
+- [ ] Post #4 live
+## Friday — Design & Repurpose
+- [ ] `/design-brief` for each approved visual
+- [ ] Produce graphics from the master templates
+- [ ] `/podcast-repurpose` if an episode was recorded
+- [ ] Schedule next week where approved
+- [ ] Update the tracking sheet
+## Monthly (last Friday)
+- [ ] Full dashboard — Tier 1, 2 and 3
+- [ ] Pillar performance review → rebalance next month's mix
+- [ ] Refresh the guest pipeline to 10 deep
+- [ ] Lead magnet production (M2+)
+- [ ] Client call: results, learnings, next month, one explicit ask
+## Approval flow
+1. Draft → `02-linkedin/post-bank/` marked `STATUS: draft`
+2. Batch of 7 sent Thursday → `STATUS: in-review`
+3. Approved → `STATUS: approved`, design brief raised
+4. Scheduled → `STATUS: scheduled` + date
+5. Published → `STATUS: live` + URL, performance logged after 72h
+**Unreturned after 48h = approved.** Agreed up front so the calendar can't be blocked
+by silence.
+## Escalation — never freelance on these
+Route to the client, don't answer: anything about regulation, securities, custody,
+tax or jurisdiction · claims about funds safety we can't source · competitor disputes ·
+anything involving a named individual · press enquiries.
+Answer ourselves, in public, with a mechanism: technical criticism, "how does this
+differ from X", scepticism about agent spending. These are our best content.

lines: +#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# UserPromptSubmit hook — appends every prompt to the project's monthly prompt log.
+# Never blocks the session: all failures exit 0 silently.
+set -uo pipefail
+INPUT=$(cat)
+ROOT="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)}"
+LOGDIR="$ROOT/vapi-network/logs/prompts"
+mkdir -p "$LOGDIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
+MONTH=$(date -u +%Y-%m)
+FILE="$LOGDIR/$MONTH.md"
+TS=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%SZ")
+SID=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.session_id // "unknown"' 2>/dev/null) || SID=unknown
+PROMPT=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.prompt // ""' 2>/dev/null) || PROMPT=""
+[ -z "$PROMPT" ] && exit 0

+[ -f "$FILE" ] || printf '# Prompt log — %s

_Appended automatically by `.claude/hooks/log-prompt.sh`._
' "$MONTH" > "$FILE"

+  printf '
---

### %s · session `%s`

' "$TS" "${SID:0:12}"
+  printf '%s\n' "$PROMPT" | sed 's/^/> /'
+exit 0
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Stop / SessionEnd hook — archives the session transcript into the project.
+Writes two things per session:
+  logs/transcripts/<date>-<sid>.jsonl   raw, complete
+  logs/transcripts/<date>-<sid>.md      readable digest of prompts + responses
+Fails silently (exit 0) so it can never block a session.
+import json, os, shutil, sys, datetime, pathlib
+def main():
+    try:
+        data = json.load(sys.stdin)
+    except Exception:
+        return
+    tp = data.get("transcript_path")
+    if not tp or not os.path.exists(tp):
+        return
+    root = pathlib.Path(
+        os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR")
+        or pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+    outdir = root / "vapi-network" / "logs" / "transcripts"
+    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    sid = (data.get("session_id") or "unknown")[:12]
+    day = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
+    stem = f"{day}-{sid}"
+    try:

{text}

{text}

Read this before any work in this folder. Full research: `01-strategy/client-profile.md`.

**vAPI Network** (`vapinetwork.ai`) — "onchain task market for agents and humans".
Non-custodial toolkit for discovering and paying x402 APIs. Products: **Call (live)**,
Tasks, Compute, Stake (not live).

**They are NOT `vapi.ai`**, the voice-AI company (YC W21, $50M Series B, 1M+ devs).
Different company. When researching, always disambiguate.

## Hard rules
1. **Only Call is live.** Never write copy implying Tasks, Compute or Stake have shipped.
   Pre-launch products get build-in-public framing only.
2. **Always "vAPI Network", never "VAPI" alone.** First line of every post, every
   watermark. This is the fix for the name collision.
3. **No invented metrics, quotes, case studies, testimonials or client results.**
   If it isn't in a file here or from a cited source, write `[NEEDS DATA: ...]`.
4. **Never publish externally without explicit per-item approval.** Drafting is safe;
   posting, DMing and scheduling are not.
5. **Never freelance on compliance.** Regulation, securities, custody, tax and
   jurisdiction questions get escalated to the client, not answered.
6. Read `01-strategy/voice-and-tone.md` before writing any copy, and check the
   banned-words list before you finish.

## Voice, in one line
A senior engineer explaining something they find genuinely interesting, to a smart
person who doesn't work in crypto. Calm, specific, no hype. No emoji bullets, no
"excited to announce", no token or price talk.

## Where things go
| | |
|---|---|
| `00-pitch/` | Meeting materials for the trial pitch |
| `01-strategy/` | Client profile, ICP, pillars, voice, KPIs, research |
| `02-linkedin/` | Calendar, post bank, templates, engagement playbook |
| `03-podcast/` | Playbook, per-episode folders, templates |
| `04-design/` | Brand guidelines, asset specs, briefs |
| `05-ops/` | Weekly workflow, chat map, reporting |
| `logs/` | Auto-captured prompts and transcripts — do not edit by hand |

## How work gets started
One job per session, via the slash commands in `.claude/commands/`.
See `05-ops/chat-map.md`.
EOF

# Logs

Everything this project's Claude Code sessions do is captured here automatically.
**Don't edit these by hand.**

| Path | What | Written by |

to fail silently — they can never block or slow a session.

```bash
ls -la vapi-network/logs/prompts vapi-network/logs/transcripts
```
If a month file exists and is growing, it's working. Transcripts are written when a
session ends, so the current session won't appear until it stops.

Transcripts contain the full text of everything discussed in a session. If client
credentials, contracts or personal data ever get pasted into a session, they land here
too. Keep this repo private, and scrub before sharing any log externally.

# Engagement Playbook

**A page with zero followers has zero distribution. Commenting is how you borrow
somebody else's.** This is half the programme and the half most agencies skip because
it doesn't produce a deliverable.

## The weekly numbers
- **Founders: 10 substantive comments per week each.** Not "great post" — 2+ sentences that add a data point, a distinction or a counter-example.
- **Company page: 5 comments per week** on ecosystem and partner posts.
- **Respond to every comment on our own posts within 2 hours.** The first 60 minutes after publishing is the highest-leverage hour of the week.

## Who to engage with

**Tier 1 — ecosystem amplifiers (ICP C).** x402 ecosystem builders, Base and Coinbase
devrel, MCP and agent-framework maintainers, AI-infra analysts and newsletter writers.
Biggest reach per comment, and this is the podcast guest pool. _Target: 8/week._

**Tier 2 — ICP A buyers.** Heads of platform, automation and AI leads, VPs of
engineering, agency owners posting about agents in production. _Target: 7/week._

**Tier 3 — ICP B supply.** API product owners, indie devs, data providers posting about
monetisation or billing pain. _Target: 5/week._

## What a good comment looks like
1. **Add a fact** — "x402 governance moved to the Linux Foundation in April with Visa and Mastercard as members, which changes the procurement conversation quite a bit."
2. **Make a distinction** — "Worth separating custodial from non-custodial here. Most agent-payment tools hold the funds; the risk profile is completely different."
3. **Offer a counter-example** — "We see the opposite in the x402 data: >80% settles on Base, almost all USDC."
4. **Ask a real question** — "How are you capping spend today? That's the part I never see a clean answer to."

## What never to do
- "Great post!" / "💯" / "This 👆"
- Pitching vAPI in a comment. Ever. The profile is the pitch.
- Correcting someone publicly in a way that embarrasses them
- Commenting on anything political, or on a competitor's bad news
- Copy-pasting the same comment across posts

## Connection requests
Send 15–20 per week, only to people whose post you've *already* commented on, with a
note referencing what they said. Never a pitch in the request.

## DMs — the rule
**Never open with a pitch.** Only DM someone who has engaged with us first, and always
reference the specific thing they engaged with. The M3 warm-DM playbook builds on this;
until then, DMs are for podcast invites and genuine replies only.

## Podcast invite = the best outreach we have
"Come on the podcast" gets a far higher reply rate than any pitch, because it's a gift
rather than an ask. Every week, 3 new invites to Tier 1 targets. Keep the guest pipeline
10 deep at all times.

## Log
Append weekly to `engagement-log.md`: who was engaged, what happened, anything that
turned into a conversation, new guest targets identified.
EOF

+# Engagement Playbook
+**A page with zero followers has zero distribution. Commenting is how you borrow
+somebody else's.** This is half the programme and the half most agencies skip because
+it doesn't produce a deliverable.
+## The weekly numbers
+- **Founders: 10 substantive comments per week each.** Not "great post" — 2+ sentences that add a data point, a distinction or a counter-example.
+- **Company page: 5 comments per week** on ecosystem and partner posts.
+- **Respond to every comment on our own posts within 2 hours.** The first 60 minutes after publishing is the highest-leverage hour of the week.
+## Who to engage with
+**Tier 1 — ecosystem amplifiers (ICP C).** x402 ecosystem builders, Base and Coinbase
+devrel, MCP and agent-framework maintainers, AI-infra analysts and newsletter writers.
+Biggest reach per comment, and this is the podcast guest pool. _Target: 8/week._
+**Tier 2 — ICP A buyers.** Heads of platform, automation and AI leads, VPs of
+engineering, agency owners posting about agents in production. _Target: 7/week._
+**Tier 3 — ICP B supply.** API product owners, indie devs, data providers posting about
+monetisation or billing pain. _Target: 5/week._
+## What a good comment looks like
+1. **Add a fact** — "x402 governance moved to the Linux Foundation in April with Visa and Mastercard as members, which changes the procurement conversation quite a bit."
+2. **Make a distinction** — "Worth separating custodial from non-custodial here. Most agent-payment tools hold the funds; the risk profile is completely different."
+3. **Offer a counter-example** — "We see the opposite in the x402 data: >80% settles on Base, almost all USDC."
+4. **Ask a real question** — "How are you capping spend today? That's the part I never see a clean answer to."
+## What never to do
+- "Great post!" / "💯" / "This 👆"
+- Pitching vAPI in a comment. Ever. The profile is the pitch.
+- Correcting someone publicly in a way that embarrasses them
+- Commenting on anything political, or on a competitor's bad news
+- Copy-pasting the same comment across posts
+## Connection requests
+Send 15–20 per week, only to people whose post you've *already* commented on, with a
+note referencing what they said. Never a pitch in the request.
+## DMs — the rule
+**Never open with a pitch.** Only DM someone who has engaged with us first, and always
+reference the specific thing they engaged with. The M3 warm-DM playbook builds on this;
+until then, DMs are for podcast invites and genuine replies only.
+## Podcast invite = the best outreach we have
+"Come on the podcast" gets a far higher reply rate than any pitch, because it's a gift
+rather than an ask. Every week, 3 new invites to Tier 1 targets. Keep the guest pipeline
+10 deep at all times.
+## Log
+Append weekly to `engagement-log.md`: who was engaged, what happened, anything that
+turned into a conversation, new guest targets identified.

# Sample Posts — written for the pitch

Three posts, three pillars, three ICPs. Show these on the call. They're the fastest way
to prove the voice is right before anyone has to trust a plan.

> Every factual claim below is sourced in `01-strategy/client-profile.md`. Nothing is invented.

---

## 1 · Trust & Control — ICP A (buyers) · text + stat card · founder profile

> Would you give an autonomous process your company card?
>
> Nobody says yes to that question. But 165 million agent payments happened on x402 last year, and almost none of them had a hard spend cap.
>
> That gap is the whole problem with agent payments right now. The tooling raced ahead of the controls.
>
> Three questions worth asking of anything you let an agent pay with:
>
> 1. Is the spend policy checked before the transaction is signed, or after it fails?
> 2. Where does the private key actually live? If the answer is "our servers", you've outsourced custody without calling it that.
> 3. Is there a receipt? Not a dashboard you can log into — a record you hold.
>
> We built vAPI Network around those three answers, because we couldn't find a tool that gave all three. Key stays encrypted on your machine. Policy applies before signing. Every payment writes to a local append-only ledger.
>
> None of that is exciting. It's just what has to be true before finance signs off.
>
> What's stopping you from letting an agent spend money today — the tech, or the audit trail?
>
> #x402 #agenticpayments #agenteconomy

**Visual:** stat card — "165,000,000 agent payments. Almost no spend caps."
**First comment:** link to the Hacken audit + the repo.
**Why it works:** opens with the reader's fear, answers with mechanisms, ends with a
question that is genuine ICP research. No product pitch until line 8.

---

## 2 · The Agent Economy — ICP A + B · carousel, 8 slides · company page

**Title:** *x402, explained for people who don't work in crypto*

| Slide | Copy |
|---|---|
| 1 | **x402, explained for people who don't work in crypto.** There's a payments standard behind AI agents. Your board has probably heard of the members. |
| 2 | HTTP has always had a status code reserved for this. **402: Payment Required.** It sat unused for about 30 years. |
| 3 | x402 finally uses it. A server answers a request with "402 — this costs $0.004." The client pays. The request goes through. No account. No login. No invoice. |
| 4 | **Why now:** agents. A human can fill in a billing form. An autonomous process at 3am cannot. |
| 5 | **Who's behind it:** Coinbase launched it in 2025. Governance moved to the **Linux Foundation in April 2026** — 22 launch members including Google, Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, AWS and Circle. |
| 6 | **The scale so far:** 69,000 active agents. 165 million transactions. Over 80% settling on Base, almost all in USDC. |
| 7 | **What it changes:** an API can be sold per request, to a machine, for fractions of a cent — with no billing page and no chasing payment. |
| 8 | vAPI Network is one wallet for every x402 API. Non-custodial, spend-capped, audited, Apache 2.0. **Link in the comments.** |

**Why it works:** vendor-neutral for 7 of 8 slides, so it travels. The Linux Foundation
slide is the one that gets screenshotted — it's what reframes this from "crypto" to
"standard". Carousels get the best dwell time on LinkedIn.

---

## 3 · Supply-Side — ICP B (sellers) · text + image · company page

> Your API made four-tenths of a cent last night, and you didn't do anything.
>
> That's the part that takes a while to get used to.
>
> If you run an API today, monetising it means a billing provider, a pricing page, a login wall, invoicing, and someone chasing a $40 invoice for three weeks. For a call worth $0.004, the overhead is comically larger than the payment.
>
> So most people don't bother. The API stays internal, or free, or behind a wall that only enterprise customers get past.
>
> x402 removes the overhead. A machine requests your endpoint, gets told the price, pays it, and gets the response. No account created. No invoice raised. Money settles directly to you in USDC.
>
> There are roughly 69,000 active agents already doing this, across 165 million transactions.
>
> vAPI Network is how they find you and pay you.
>
> If you've got an API sitting behind a login wall because billing wasn't worth the effort — that reason expired.
>
> What would you list first?
>
> #x402 #apimonetization #agenteconomy

**Visual:** simple receipt graphic — one line item, `$0.004`, 03:41 UTC, settled.
**Why it works:** concrete scene as the hook, names the exact operational pain the ICP
lives with, and the close is a low-friction question rather than a demo request.
EOF

# Podcast Playbook

## Why it exists
Not for downloads. For three things, in this order:

1. **Content supply.** One 45-minute recording → 8–12 LinkedIn assets. It's the cheapest content we will ever make.
2. **Business development.** The invite list *is* the target list. "Come on the podcast" gets a reply where a cold DM gets deleted, because it's a gift rather than an ask.
3. **Borrowed authority.** A zero-follower page sitting next to a recognised ecosystem name inherits some of their credibility, and their repost reaches their audience.

Downloads are a lagging vanity metric here. Judge it on clips published, guest quality
and guest→network conversion.

## Format
- **45 minutes**, video + audio. Video is non-negotiable — it's where the clips come from.
- **Fortnightly** for months 1–2, weekly in month 3 if the pipeline supports it.
- One guest per episode. One clear angle per episode.
- Conversational, not interrogative. The host should disagree occasionally.
- Remote, recorded locally both ends (Riverside/Zencastr class tooling).

## Guest tiers
**Tier 1 — ecosystem builders (ICP C).** x402 projects, Base/Coinbase devrel, MCP and
agent-framework maintainers, AI-infra writers. Best reach, most likely to amplify.

**Tier 2 — practitioners (ICP A).** People running agents in production — agency owners,
platform leads, automation heads. **These episodes are sales calls that neither side has
to call a sales call.** Start booking these in month 3.

**Tier 3 — adjacent authority.** Security researchers, payments people, open-source
maintainers. Best for the Trust & Control pillar.

Keep the pipeline **10 deep at all times.** The best source of guest #7 is guest #5 —
always ask, on the recording, "who should we have on next?"

## The loop
```
target list (10 deep)
  → invite (reference their specific work; never a template)
  → 15-min pre-call (angle, clip targets, what they don't want asked)
  → record 45 min
  → edit + clip within 72h
  → guest reviews their clips before publish  ← builds goodwill, guarantees the repost
  → publish + 8–12 assets over 2 weeks
  → ask for the referral
```

## Per-episode asset set
| # | Asset |
|---|---|
| 1 | Episode announce + guest quote card |
| 2–5 | 4 × clips, 45–90s, captioned, 4:5 |
| 6 | Carousel — "N things [guest] taught us about X" |
| 7–8 | 2 × quote cards, verbatim only |
| 9 | Founder text post — the one thing that changed their mind |
| 10 | Repost copy handed to the guest |
| 11 | Audiogram / teaser |
| 12 | Newsletter / article version |

## Clip selection — what actually travels
- A strong opinion stated plainly
- A specific number with a story attached
- A disagreement, or a corrected assumption
- A concrete anecdote — "we lost $4,000 in an afternoon because..."
- **Never** the polite intro, the credentials recap, or anything needing setup to make sense

Hook in the **first 1.5 seconds**. Burned-in captions always — most of LinkedIn watches muted.

## Distribution
LinkedIn first (that's the brief). Then YouTube for search and embeds, then the audio
feeds. The guest's own repost matters more than any of them.

## Metrics
Downloads/episode · completion rate · **clips published per episode (target ≥8)** ·
guest→network conversion · guest referral rate · LinkedIn impressions from podcast-derived assets.
EOF

+- One guest per episode. One clear angle per episode.
+- Conversational, not interrogative. The host should disagree occasionally.
+- Remote, recorded locally both ends (Riverside/Zencastr class tooling).
+## Guest tiers
+**Tier 1 — ecosystem builders (ICP C).** x402 projects, Base/Coinbase devrel, MCP and
+agent-framework maintainers, AI-infra writers. Best reach, most likely to amplify.
+**Tier 2 — practitioners (ICP A).** People running agents in production — agency owners,
+platform leads, automation heads. **These episodes are sales calls that neither side has
+to call a sales call.** Start booking these in month 3.
+**Tier 3 — adjacent authority.** Security researchers, payments people, open-source
+maintainers. Best for the Trust & Control pillar.
+Keep the pipeline **10 deep at all times.** The best source of guest #7 is guest #5 —
+always ask, on the recording, "who should we have on next?"
+## The loop
+target list (10 deep)
+  → invite (reference their specific work; never a template)
+  → 15-min pre-call (angle, clip targets, what they don't want asked)
+  → record 45 min
+  → edit + clip within 72h
+  → guest reviews their clips before publish  ← builds goodwill, guarantees the repost
+  → publish + 8–12 assets over 2 weeks
+  → ask for the referral
+## Per-episode asset set
+| # | Asset |
+| 1 | Episode announce + guest quote card |
+| 2–5 | 4 × clips, 45–90s, captioned, 4:5 |
+| 6 | Carousel — "N things [guest] taught us about X" |
+| 7–8 | 2 × quote cards, verbatim only |
+| 9 | Founder text post — the one thing that changed their mind |
+| 10 | Repost copy handed to the guest |
+| 11 | Audiogram / teaser |
+| 12 | Newsletter / article version |
+## Clip selection — what actually travels
+- A strong opinion stated plainly
+- A specific number with a story attached
+- A disagreement, or a corrected assumption
+- A concrete anecdote — "we lost $4,000 in an afternoon because..."
+- **Never** the polite intro, the credentials recap, or anything needing setup to make sense
+Hook in the **first 1.5 seconds**. Burned-in captions always — most of LinkedIn watches muted.
+## Distribution
+LinkedIn first (that's the brief). Then YouTube for search and embeds, then the audio
+feeds. The guest's own repost matters more than any of them.
+## Metrics
+Downloads/episode · completion rate · **clips published per episode (target ≥8)** ·
+guest→network conversion · guest referral rate · LinkedIn impressions from podcast-derived assets.

# Brand Guidelines — working version

> `[NEEDS ASSETS]` Logo files, fonts and colour hexes to be supplied by the client.
> Everything below is the **working system** until then. Confirm on the handover call.

## The look, in one line
**Technical, restrained, high-contrast.** Closer to developer documentation than to a
crypto project. The visual job is to make "onchain" feel like infrastructure, not
speculation.

Reference points: Stripe docs, Linear, Vercel. **Not:** gradient meshes, glowing orbs,
3D coins, neon purple, rocket ships.

## Colour `[NEEDS CLIENT HEXES]`
| Role | Use |
|---|---|
| Primary | Headlines, key data points, the one thing the eye should hit first |
| Ink | Body text. Near-black, not pure black |
| Surface | Backgrounds. Near-white or near-black — pick one and be consistent |
| Accent | One only, used sparingly, for emphasis |
| Muted | Secondary text, labels, captions |

**Rule: one accent colour per asset.** Two accents reads as a slide from 2014.
**Contrast minimum 4.5:1** for all body text, verified per asset.

## Type `[NEEDS CLIENT FONTS]`
- **Display:** geometric or neo-grotesque sans. Tight tracking on headlines.
- **Body:** the same family, regular weight.
- **Mono:** for anything code, numeric or receipt-like. This is the signature move for
  a product about machine payments — use it deliberately.
- Maximum **two weights** per asset.

## Layout
- Generous margins. Empty space reads as confidence.
- Strict left alignment. Centred text only on quote cards.
- Text must be **legible at thumbnail size** — that's how most people first see it.
- One idea per asset. If it needs two, it's two assets.

## Watermark — mandatory
**"vAPI Network"** on every asset, bottom-left or bottom-right, muted colour, small but
readable. This is a direct mitigation for the `vapi.ai` name collision: assets get
screenshotted and reshared without the post, and the watermark is the only thing that
travels with them.

## Never
- Stock photos of people shaking hands, or anything from a "business" stock set
- 3D coins, tokens, rockets, moons, bulls
- Gradient-on-gradient
- More than 25 words on a static image
- Text over a busy photo
- Emoji as design elements
EOF

# Week 0 Checklist — run this the day the trial is green-lit

Nothing publishes this week. This is the foundation, and skipping it is why most
LinkedIn launches stall around week five.

## Day 1 — Access & assets
- [ ] LinkedIn company page admin access granted
- [ ] Brand assets received: logo (SVG + PNG), fonts, colour hexes, existing deck
- [ ] Named content approver confirmed + 48h turnaround agreed
- [ ] Shared folder / Notion / Slack channel set up
- [ ] Analytics access: page, website, CRM
- [ ] CRM field created for LinkedIn-sourced leads

## Day 1–2 — Fix the name problem _(do this first, it's free and time-sensitive)_
- [ ] Page name set to **"vAPI Network"** — never "VAPI" alone
- [ ] **Custom page URL claimed** before someone else takes it
- [ ] Tagline includes "onchain task market" so link previews disambiguate
- [ ] About section keyword-weighted: x402, agent payments, AI agent infrastructure, USDC, non-custodial
- [ ] Hashtag set locked: `#x402` `#agenticpayments` `#agenteconomy`. Never `#vapi`
- [ ] Standard bio line drafted for every employee profile

## Day 2–3 — Page & profiles
- [ ] Company page: banner, logo, tagline, About, Products, custom CTA button
- [ ] **Founder/exec profile overhauls** (≥2): headline, banner, About, Featured
- [ ] Founders briefed on the commenting routine (10/week) and shown how it works
- [ ] Employee advocacy list drawn up

## Day 3–4 — Design system
- [ ] 6 master templates built: quote, stat, carousel cover, carousel interior, clip frame, podcast announce
- [ ] Watermark placement locked
- [ ] Page banner + founder banners produced
- [ ] Contrast + thumbnail legibility checked on all six

## Day 4–5 — Content & podcast
- [ ] **30-day calendar drafted and approved in one batch** — so weeks 1–4 never wait on sign-off
- [ ] First 7 posts fully drafted
- [ ] Engagement target list built (20 accounts across ICP A/B/C)
- [ ] Podcast: name, cover art, format, recording stack
- [ ] **Guest pipeline 10 deep**, first 3 invites sent
- [ ] Tracking sheet live, baseline recorded

# Session 01 — Project setup & pitch preparation
**Date:** 2026-09-20 · **Goal:** stand up the project folder and prepare tomorrow's agency pitch

## What was asked
Build a dedicated project folder for the vAPI Network trial (LinkedIn from scratch,
podcast management, graphic design), structured so different tasks run in different
sessions, with full prompt/output logging — and prepare a 3-month plan to pitch in a
30-minute meeting tomorrow.

## Research findings (the two that changed the approach)

**1. vapinetwork.ai is not what the brief implied.** It's an **onchain task market for
agents and humans** — a non-custodial toolkit for discovering and paying x402 APIs.
Products: Call (live), Tasks, Compute, Stake (not live). Web3 × AI-agent infrastructure,
not a recruitment platform. "Recruitment to the platform" reads as **two-sided market
supply/demand acquisition**, and the whole content strategy is built on that split.

**2. There's a severe name collision.** `vapi.ai` — voice AI, YC W21, $50M Series B in
May 2026, 1M+ developers — owns every "VAPI" search on LinkedIn, where search is
name-match weighted. This is a real commercial problem with a free fix, and it became
the opening move of the pitch.

Supporting: x402 governance moved to the **Linux Foundation in April 2026** (Google, Visa,
Mastercard, Stripe, AWS, Circle). 69,000 active agents, 165M transactions. This is the
"it's a standard, not a crypto toy" ammunition that makes the category legible to a
LinkedIn B2B audience.

_Note: `vapinetwork.ai` itself is blocked by this environment's egress proxy. Findings
came from the GitHub repo, search results and ecosystem sources — all cited in
`01-strategy/client-profile.md`. **Verify the homepage copy directly before the meeting.**_

## What was built
- Full project folder: `00-pitch/` → `05-ops/`, plus `logs/`
- Pitch pack: 30-minute run-sheet, 90-day plan, scope & pricing, objection handling, discovery questions, 3 sample posts
- Strategy: client profile, ICP & positioning, content pillars, voice & tone, KPI framework with honest target bands
- Ops: weekly workflow, chat map, Week-0 checklist, reporting templates
- 8 slash commands in `.claude/commands/` — one per recurring job
- Automatic logging hooks (prompts + transcripts), both smoke-tested

## Open questions for the client call
Tracked in `00-pitch/discovery-questions.md`. The two that most affect scope:
- Is $1,300 monthly or for the whole 90 days?
- Will founders post from personal profiles? _(Determines whether the target bands are realistic.)_
EOF

Done — 50 files, committed and pushed to `claude/vapi-linkedin-podcast-setup-cc75a4`.

## Read this before tomorrow — the brief doesn't match the client

**vapinetwork.ai is not a recruitment platform.** It's an *"onchain task market for agents and humans"* — a non-custodial toolkit that lets AI agents discover and pay for APIs over the x402 protocol. Products: **Call (live today)**, Tasks, Compute, Stake (all pre-launch).

Your framing still works, but it means something different. "Bring B2B businesses so they can bring recruitment to the platform" = **two-sided marketplace acquisition**: recruit buyers (companies whose agents need to spend money) *and* suppliers (API providers, dev shops, specialists who get paid). The whole content strategy is built on that split with a fixed ratio.

One caveat: **their homepage is blocked by this environment's egress proxy.** Everything came from their GitHub, search results and ecosystem sources — all cited in `01-strategy/client-profile.md`. Open the site yourself tonight and check I've got it right.

## Your opening move

`vapi.ai` — voice AI, YC W21, **$50M Series B in May 2026**, 1M+ developers — owns every "VAPI" search on LinkedIn, where search is name-match weighted. vAPI Network is invisible behind them.

It's a real commercial problem, the fix is free, and it takes 90 seconds. It proves you did the work before you've claimed anything. Everything after lands on a receptive room.

The supporting fact that reframes the whole category for a LinkedIn audience: **x402 governance moved to the Linux Foundation in April 2026** — Google, Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, AWS, Circle. That's what turns "crypto thing" into "standard my board has heard of," and nobody is telling that story on LinkedIn.

## What's in the folder

- **`00-pitch/`** — run-sheet, 90-day plan, scope/pricing, objections, discovery questions, 3 sample posts
- **`01-strategy/`** — sourced client profile, ICP, five content pillars, voice guide, KPIs
- **`02-linkedin/` `03-podcast/` `04-design/`** — playbooks, templates, specs
- **`05-ops/`** — weekly rhythm, chat map, Week-0 checklist, reporting templates

**The infrastructure you asked for:** 8 slash commands in `.claude/commands/` (`/weekly-content`, `/engage`, `/podcast-prep`, `/podcast-repurpose`, `/design-brief`, `/report`, `/research`, `/post-draft`) — one per recurring job, so each task runs in its own clean session. Plus hooks that archive **every prompt and every transcript** to `vapi-network/logs/`. Both smoke-tested and working; I cleaned up the test files.

## Three things I need from you

1. **Is $1,300 monthly or for the whole 90 days?** Scope doc has both columns. Settle it early in the call — it's a 3× difference in deliverables.
2. **The claude.ai Project I can't create for you** — that's a UI action. `05-ops/setup-and-linking.md` has both routes (Desktop local folder, or connect the pushed repo). Worth knowing: the automatic logging is a Claude Code feature and won't capture chats held in a web Project.
3. **The founder condition.** LinkedIn suppresses company-page reach — personal profiles get 5–20× the reach at the same follower count. I've written the target bands to depend on ≥2 founders posting, and the run-sheet has you say that out loud in the room. Don't soften it. Missing it in month two is much worse than naming it now.

I also wrote in kill criteria — if week 6 is under 2% engagement with zero qualified conversations, you stop and re-plan. Offering that yourself reads as confidence, not hedging.

Want me to turn the 90-day plan into a shareable web page you can pull up on the call instead of screen-sharing a markdown file?
